claims.claim: In 1801 Lockwood, a new tenant, visits his landlord Heathcliff at Wuthering Heights
claims.evidence: 'Mr. Lockwood, your new tenant'; 'Thrushcross Grange is my own, sir'

claims.claim: Heights is on the Yorkshire moors; Heathcliff gruff, household unwelcoming
claims.evidence: 'closed teeth ... Go to the Deuce!'

claims.claim: A snowstorm traps Lockwood there overnight
claims.evidence: 'The snow began to drive thickly' ... he stays the night

claims.claim: Mr. Earnshaw brings the orphan Heathcliff home
claims.evidence: 'Liverpool ... gipsy brat'; 'in the streets of Liverpool, where he picked it up'

claims.claim: Heathcliff and Catherine grow close
claims.evidence: Catherine: 'I am Heathcliff'; locked up Heathcliff, dancing scene

claims.claim: Hindley abuses/degrades Heathcliff
claims.evidence: 'Heathcliff bore his degradation pretty well at first'

claims.claim: Catherine marries wealthy Edgar Linton of Thrushcross Grange
claims.evidence: Catherine becomes Mrs. Linton

claims.claim: Heathcliff leaves and returns rich
claims.evidence: 'absent and silent for three years'; Nelly: 'how has he got rich?'

claims.claim: He marries Isabella to hurt the Lintons
claims.evidence: searched Isabella/revenge passages; motive not stated in any passage I read; marriage itself confirmed ('Mrs. Heathcliff')

claims.claim: Catherine dies after giving birth to daughter Cathy
claims.evidence: 'was born the Catherine ... and two hours after the mother died'

claims.claim: Heathcliff gains the Heights and the Grange
claims.evidence: Hindley mortgaged all to Heathcliff; Grange claimed 'in his wife's right and his also'

claims.claim: Heathcliff tyrannizes Hareton and the younger generation
claims.evidence: Hareton in the kitchen, Cathy and Linton imprisoned

claims.claim: Heathcliff forces Cathy to marry his sickly son Linton
claims.evidence: Heathcliff locks them up: 'I'll marry him within this hour'; 'an ailing, peevish creature'

claims.claim: Linton dies
claims.evidence: Heathcliff 'let her be till after the funeral'; 'Mrs. Heathcliff ... He's safe, and I'm free'

claims.claim: Heathcliff weakens and dies
claims.evidence: death confirmed ('he was dead and stark!'); weakening not read
claims.fix: Heathcliff himself is later found dead

claims.claim: Cathy and Hareton fall in love and plan to marry
claims.evidence: 'as soon as they are married, and that will be on New Year's Day'

claims.claim: Nelly Dean tells the story to Lockwood
claims.evidence: Mrs. Dean narrates throughout

claims.claim: Heathcliff is a foundling raised at Wuthering Heights; vengeful
claims.evidence: as above

claims.claim: Hindley Earnshaw is Catherine's brother; Hareton is Hindley's son
claims.evidence: 'Young Earnshaw'; 'my cousin Hareton'

claims.claim: Edgar is gentle master of Thrushcross Grange; Cathy is Catherine's daughter
claims.evidence: as above

claims.claim: Mr. Lockwood three headstones: Edgar, Catherine, Heathcliff (end)
claims.evidence: 'the three headstones on the slope next the moor'
